title: Path of Exile 2 0.1.0 Early Access Launch: 6 Classes, 12 Ascendancies, 3 Acts and How It Differs From Current
summary: Path of Exile 2 entered Early Access on 2024-12-06 with six base classes, twelve ascendancies, a three-act campaign and a standalone endgame. This page explains exactly what 0.1.0 shipped, why Day-1 builds no longer match the current client, and which systems were later replaced by 0.2 to 0.5.
description: A complete history of the Path of Exile 2 0.1.0 Early Access launch. Covers the six launch classes and twelve ascendancies, the three-act campaign, the original Atlas and endgame, the first week of balance hotfixes, and which 0.1.0 systems are still current in client 0.5.4e versus what later patches rewrote.
author: StratLore Editorial

currentSummary: The six 0.1.0 classes remain, but the Huntress (0.2.0) and Druid (0.4.0) joined later, changing the roster and ascendancy map.
The campaign is now longer; Act 4 and the Interludes arrived in 0.3.0.
The 0.1.0 Atlas was rebuilt repeatedly through 0.2 to 0.5; current map rules differ from launch.

sections.title: Quick summary
paragraphs: Path of Exile 2 launched in Early Access on 6 December 2024 with client version 0.1.0. It opened with six base classes, twelve ascendancies, a three-act campaign and a standalone endgame built around the Atlas of Worlds. For players coming from Path of Exile 1, this was a new game with new systems rather than an extension of the old one.

The launch was deliberately a foundation. Within the first three days the team was already adjusting clearly overtuned skills such as Supercharged Slam, Magnetic Salvo and the Gas Cloud interactions, which set the tone for a launch week full of rapid hotfixes.

This page is the total-entry history for 0.1.0: what shipped at launch, how the first week stabilised, and which parts of 0.1.0 are still recognisable in client 0.5.4e versus what later patches rewrote. Anything we could not confirm against the current client is flagged as unknown rather than guessed.

paragraphs: 0.1.0 is a historical baseline, not a current玩法 guide. The classes, ascendancies and endgame systems it introduced were the starting point, and several were expanded or replaced within the first year of Early Access.

Reading a Day-1 build video today is misleading: the skill numbers, ascendancy nodes and Atlas rules it shows were changed by launch-week hotfixes and then again by 0.2, 0.3, 0.4 and 0.5. Treat 0.1.0 footage as a record of the launch state, not as a current tutorial.

sections.title: What Early Access actually shipped
paragraphs: The launch confirmed the six base classes players still recognise: Sorceress, Warrior, Ranger, Witch, Mercenary and Monk. Each launched with two ascendancies, giving twelve total at 0.1.0 before any later class was added.

The campaign covered three acts and led into a separate endgame. That endgame already had its own Atlas, maps, league mechanics and pinnacle structure, so 0.1.0 was a complete loop rather than a vertical slice.

sections.title: Class and ascendancy map at launch

cards.detail: Both 0.1.0 Sorceress ascendancies remain; later classes added new options but did not remove these.
The two Warrior ascendancies from launch are unchanged in identity through 0.5.4e.
Ranger launched with Deadeye and Pathfinder; bow and poison archetypes trace back here.
The Witch ascendancies power the ED Contagion Lich and similar casters still played today.
Crossbow and attribute-stacking directions originated with these two Mercenary ascendancies.
The Monk ascendancies anchor quarterstaff and chaos/physical melee builds.

sections.title: Launch volatility: Day-1 vs current
sections.oldText: Several skills shipped clearly overtuned. Supercharged Slam, Magnetic Salvo and the Gas Grenade / Gas Arrow / Flame Wall ignite loops dominated early footage, and some Day-1 builds looked dramatically stronger than they would within days.
sections.newText: 0.1.0b and the surrounding hotfixes pulled Gas Grenade and Gas Arrow explosion damage down, and the team kept watching clear outliers. By 0.2 to 0.5 the numbers had moved again, so the current client bears little resemblance to launch balance.

cards.detail: The 0.1.0 Atlas had Waystones, Towers, Tablets and Citadels in early forms that later patches restructured.
Breach, Expedition, Ritual and Delirium entered maps at launch; their current behaviour was tuned in later patches.
Early pinnacle access had a steeper retry cost than later patches introduced recovery for.
Waystone tiering and prefixes were adjusted in 0.1.0c and many times after; old sustain advice is outdated.

rows.currentSummary: All six 0.1.0 classes are still playable in 0.5.4e, now alongside later additions.
The twelve ascendancies are still selectable and unchanged in identity.
The campaign is longer now; Acts beyond the original three arrived in 0.3.0.
Map and Waystone systems were rebuilt through 0.2 to 0.5; launch-era sustain advice no longer applies.

entries.takeaway: Official reveal of the 0.1.0 class and endgame direction. Read alongside the launch-hotfix notes for what changed in the first week.
entries.creator: Official Path of Exile 2

items.question: Was 0.1.0 the finished game?
answer: No. 0.1.0 was the Early Access foundation: six classes, twelve ascendancies, a three-act campaign and a standalone endgame. Large content and system expansions followed in 0.2 to 0.5.

items.question: Why do my Day-1 build videos feel different now?
answer: Launch-week hotfixes (starting with 0.1.0b) already changed clear outliers, and 0.2 to 0.5 moved the numbers again. Trust current build pages over launch recordings.

items.question: Which 0.1.0 systems are still current in 0.5.4e?
answer: The six launch classes and twelve ascendancies are still current. The campaign and Atlas were expanded or rebuilt, so those parts no longer match launch footage.

items.question: Why does the site keep historical 0.1.0 pages?
answer: Players still search for what launched and how it evolved. Keeping sourced historical pages helps returning players understand why old videos no longer match the client.
